## Natural history notes

A medium-sized paper wasp characterized by its slender reddish-brown body, long dangling legs, narrow waist, and yellow markings on the face, thorax, or abdomen. In Florida, it is found in gardens, fields, forest edges, parks, yards, wetlands, and around buildings where sheltered nesting sites are available. It builds open, umbrella-shaped paper nests under branches, eaves, railings, or other protected surfaces, and adults hunt caterpillars and other soft-bodied insects to feed their larvae while also visiting flowers for nectar.
